final_candidates.decision_summary: Modifying the V3-base glycan cluster remodels recognition by glycan-dependent antibodies while generally retaining core Env function better than full glycan-supersite ablation. Lower confidence due to uncertain net escape direction without structural evidence.

stop_reason.detail: No external evidence tools are available and the pool has converged after self-review, so further rounds would not improve the Top-3.

history.rationale: Removes the conserved N-linked glycan at the V3 base (part of the high-mannose supersite), a well-established escape mechanism against glycan-dependent bnAbs while the local structure is loop-exposed and tolerates substitution.

Removing a conserved PNGS generally exposes rather than shields neutralizing epitopes, which is directionally opposite to increased antibody escape; fitness/folding risk is nonzero. Reject as misaligned with the reward.

rejection.reason: Removing a conserved PNGS generally exposes rather than shields neutralizing epitopes, which is directionally opposite to increased antibody escape; fitness/folding risk is nonzero. Reject as misaligned with the reward.

history.rationale: Eliminates the gp41 WNSS glycan site in the gp120-gp41 interface epitope region, conferring escape from interface-targeting antibodies; conservative N-to-Q preserves polarity.
gp41 N-glycan changes can modulate MPER/HR accessibility, but direction is uncertain; keep at low confidence pending self-review.
Removes a V1/V2 glycan that shields the trimer apex, likely reducing recognition by apex-directed antibodies; N-to-Q is sterically conservative.
Deglycosylation in the V1/V2 region tends to increase neutralization sensitivity and can perturb trimer glycan shield, so it likely reduces escape. Reject.

rejection.reason: Deglycosylation in the V1/V2 region tends to increase neutralization sensitivity and can perturb trimer glycan shield, so it likely reduces escape. Reject.

history.rationale: Removes a V4-region PNGS, altering glycan shielding of a highly immunogenic variable loop and promoting escape; variable loops typically tolerate substitution.
Loss of the V4 glycan shield is associated with greater antibody accessibility, not escape, and may affect folding. Reject as reward-opposed.

rejection.reason: Loss of the V4 glycan shield is associated with greater antibody accessibility, not escape, and may affect folding. Reject as reward-opposed.

history.rationale: Removes the V4/V5-edge glycan sequon, modulating shielding on the trimer side; conservative change at an exposed loop position.
Deglycosylation near CD4bs/V5 is more likely to sensitize than protect and risks conformational effects. Reject.

rejection.reason: Deglycosylation near CD4bs/V5 is more likely to sensitize than protect and risks conformational effects. Reject.

history.rationale: Eliminates a V2/C2 glycan involved in surface shielding; escape benefit with a conservative substitution at a surface-exposed site.
Removing glycan coverage is not a credible single-mutation route to escape in BG505. Reject.

rejection.reason: Removing glycan coverage is not a credible single-mutation route to escape in BG505. Reject.

history.rationale: Removes the C2 glycan near the V3 base, weakening glycan-dependent neutralization; located in a flexible region tolerant of mutation.
Shield-thinning substitution inconsistent with the escape objective. Reject.

rejection.reason: Shield-thinning substitution inconsistent with the escape objective. Reject.

history.rationale: Removes the GNNT glycan in the C3/V4-proximal region, altering an antibody-accessible glycan cluster with a conservative change.
Glycan loss near V3/C3 region likely increases vulnerability to glycan-dependent bnAbs. Reject.

rejection.reason: Glycan loss near V3/C3 region likely increases vulnerability to glycan-dependent bnAbs. Reject.

history.rationale: Removes a V1 glycan, shifting the glycan shield over variable loops implicated in neutralization escape.
V1 glycan removal is expected to expose apex/V2 epitopes and reduce escape. Reject.

rejection.reason: V1 glycan removal is expected to expose apex/V2 epitopes and reduce escape. Reject.

history.rationale: Alters the MPER epitope recognized by broadly neutralizing antibodies such as 4E10, but carries some risk to membrane-proximal function and fusion fitness.
gp41 cytoplasmic/MPER-proximal changes can affect antibody accessibility to membrane-proximal epitopes, but fitness risk is high; keep low.
Altering the V3 base glycan cluster can remodel recognition by glycan-dependent antibodies while often retaining core Env function better than N332 loss.
